audit.why: Both layers already read Skill / Zaahen / Zaahen / Skill / Skill / Zaahen / Zaahen, matching the packet chart and a 56.99% win rate over 1960 games. The two layers agree with each other and with the whys[] text.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says 'when Decimating Smash is down' eleven times without ever giving the number, and Sion's other windows are unnumbered.
audit.why: Decimating Smash is 10s at rank 1 and only stuns at full charge, Roar of the Slayer is 12s, Soul Furnace 15s, Unstoppable Onslaught 140s at rank 1. Zaahen's Q and E are both 10s at rank 1, so his pattern comes back on the same clock as Sion's Q.
audit.corrected: Number the Q at 10s and note the full-charge requirement, so 'wait for it' becomes a count rather than a vibe.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single biggest fact about fighting Sion is absent: Glory in Death reanimates him after he dies, with rapid attacks that heal him and deal bonus damage based on your maximum health. Nothing on the page mentions it, and the anti-heal line is generic. Also absent: Soul Furnace re-fires after 3 seconds, Roar of the Slayer shreds Armor, and Zaahen's E is called 'Golden Onslaught' rather than Aureate Rush.
audit.why: Riot's text for the passive: 'After being killed, Sion will temporarily reanimate... His attacks become very rapid, heal him, and deal bonus damage based on his target's maximum Health.' Two missing-interaction rules land here: needs-antiheal and resistances-invalidated. Armour is the wrong buy against max-health damage, and Grievous Wounds has to exist before the first kill, not after.
audit.corrected: State the revive and time the Grievous Wounds to before he first dies; note that Aureate Rush's percent-health damage punishes his Soul Furnace health stacking rather than being blunted by it.

audit.why: The packet flags wants.foe[2] 'Using Unstoppable Onslaught' as a probable wrong name. It is correct — the kit confirms Unstoppable Onslaught is Sion's R. False positive; left alone.

edits.after: Q is 10s at rank 1 — full charge knocks up; step in once it releases.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.

edits.before: Coin-flipping into an unknown matchup — respect what you have not seen until you have seen it twice.

edits.before: You own the early lane: Sion is slow and immobile, so you can walk up on Darkin Glaive (Q) and Golden Onslaught (E) whenever his Decimating Smash (Q) is down and freely stack damage. His only kill tool is a fully-charged Q — sidestep it and the trade is always yours.
edits.after: You own the early lane: Sion is slow and immobile, so you can walk up with The Darkin Glaive (Q, 10s) and Aureate Rush (E, 10s) whenever Decimating Smash is down and stack damage freely. His Q only stuns at full charge — step out of the wind-up and the trade is yours.

edits.before: You stay ahead — with your first item your Darkin Glaive (Q) and Cultivation of War (P) healing let you out-trade his tanky farm, and his passive-heavy playstyle means he can't fight you back if you dodge Q. Deny his farm and keep him passive.
edits.after: You stay ahead — Aureate Rush scales with his health, so Soul Furnace stacking makes him a bigger target, not a safer one. Buy Grievous Wounds before you first kill him: Glory in Death revives him and his attacks heal off your max health.

edits.before: Level 2 is already yours — Sion is immobile and reliant on charging Decimating Smash (Q), so you walk up with Darkin Glaive (Q) and Golden Onslaught (E), punish him off the wave, and only respect the charged knock-up.
edits.after: Level 2 is already yours — Sion is immobile and needs a full Decimating Smash (Q, 10s) charge to stun, so walk up with The Darkin Glaive and Aureate Rush, punish him off the wave, and step out of the wind-up.

edits.before: With items you remain the better sidelaner — Sion is a wave-clear engage tank, not a 1v1 duelist, so your Q burst and Final Retribution (R) beat him one-on-one; just sidestep his Roar of the Slayer (E) slow so he can never land a charged Q, and kill him before his ult reaches a fight.
edits.after: With items you remain the better sidelaner — Sion is a wave-clear engage tank, not a duelist, so your Q burst and R beat him one-on-one; sidestep Roar of the Slayer (E) so he never lands a charged Q, and carry Grievous Wounds because Glory in Death brings him back healing off every attack.

notes: The chart was already correct and consistent across both layers, so no chart edits. Biggest gap: Sion's Glory in Death revive was nowhere on the page, which makes the timing of Grievous Wounds (before the first kill, not after) the most valuable addition here. The packet's suspectName warning on 'Unstoppable Onslaught' is a false positive — the kit confirms the name.
